@@ -0,0 +1,138 @@
+"""
+This module contains data types used by Scrapy which are not included in the
+Python Standard Library.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import collections
+import contextlib
+import weakref
+from collections import OrderedDict
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, TypeVar, cast
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from collections.abc import Container
+
+    # typing.Self requires Python 3.11
+    from typing_extensions import Self
+
+
+_KT = TypeVar("_KT")
+_VT = TypeVar("_VT")
+
+
+class CaseInsensitiveDict(collections.UserDict[str | bytes, Any]):
+    """A dict-like structure that accepts strings or bytes
+    as keys and allows case-insensitive lookups.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
+        self._keys: dict[str | bytes, Any] = {}
+        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    def __getitem__(self, key: str | bytes) -> Any:
+        normalized_key = self._normkey(key)
+        return super().__getitem__(self._keys[normalized_key.lower()])
+
+    def __setitem__(self, key: str | bytes, value: Any) -> None:
+        normalized_key = self._normkey(key)
+        try:
+            lower_key = self._keys[normalized_key.lower()]
+            del self[lower_key]
+        except KeyError:
+            pass
+        super().__setitem__(normalized_key, self._normvalue(value))
+        self._keys[normalized_key.lower()] = normalized_key
+
+    def __delitem__(self, key: str | bytes) -> None:
+        normalized_key = self._normkey(key)
+        stored_key = self._keys.pop(normalized_key.lower())
+        super().__delitem__(stored_key)
+
+    def __contains__(self, key: str | bytes) -> bool:  # type: ignore[override]
+        normalized_key = self._normkey(key)
+        return normalized_key.lower() in self._keys
+
+    def __repr__(self) -> str:
+        return f"<{self.__class__.__name__}: {super().__repr__()}>"
+
+    # UserDict.copy() shallow-copies the instance, which would share self._keys
+    # between the copy and the original.
+    def __copy__(self) -> Self:
+        new = self.__class__()
+        new.data = self.data.copy()
+        new._keys = self._keys.copy()
+        return new

@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+"""
+pprint and pformat wrappers with colorization support
+"""
+
+import ctypes
+import platform
+import sys
+from pprint import pformat as pformat_
+from typing import Any
+
+from packaging.version import Version as parse_version
+
+
+def _enable_windows_terminal_processing() -> bool:
+    # https://stackoverflow.com/a/36760881
+    kernel32 = ctypes.windll.kernel32  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+    return bool(kernel32.SetConsoleMode(kernel32.GetStdHandle(-11), 7))
+
+
+def _tty_supports_color() -> bool:
+    if sys.platform != "win32":
+        return True
+
+    if parse_version(platform.version()) < parse_version("10.0.14393"):
+        return True
+
+    # Windows >= 10.0.14393 interprets ANSI escape sequences providing terminal
+    # processing is enabled.
+    return _enable_windows_terminal_processing()
+
+
+def _colorize(text: str, colorize: bool = True) -> str:
+    # pylint: disable=no-name-in-module
+    if not colorize or not sys.stdout.isatty() or not _tty_supports_color():
+        return text
+    try:
+        from pygments import highlight  # noqa: PLC0415
+    except ImportError:
+        return text
+    from pygments.formatters import TerminalFormatter  # noqa: PLC0415
+    from pygments.lexers import PythonLexer  # noqa: PLC0415
+
+    return highlight(text, PythonLexer(), TerminalFormatter())
+
+
+def pformat(obj: Any, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
+    return _colorize(pformat_(obj), kwargs.pop("colorize", True))
+
+
+def pprint(obj: Any, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
+    print(pformat(obj, *args, **kwargs))
diff --git a/scrapy/utils/_ftp.py b/scrapy/utils/_ftp.py
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..f08e5303d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scrapy/utils/_ftp.py
@@ -0,0 +1,53 @@
+import posixpath
+from contextlib import closing
+from ftplib import FTP, FTP_TLS, error_perm
+from posixpath import dirname
+from ssl import create_default_context
+from typing import IO
+
+
+def ftp_makedirs_cwd(ftp: FTP, path: str, first_call: bool = True) -> None:
+    """Set the current directory of the FTP connection given in the ``ftp``
+    argument (as a ftplib.FTP object), creating all parent directories if they
+    don't exist. The ftplib.FTP object must be already connected and logged in.
+    """
+    try:
+        ftp.cwd(path)
+    except error_perm:
+        ftp_makedirs_cwd(ftp, dirname(path), False)
+        ftp.mkd(path)
+        if first_call:
+            ftp.cwd(path)
+
+
+def ftp_store_file(
+    *,
+    path: str,
+    file: IO[bytes],
+    host: str,
+    port: int,
+    username: str,
+    password: str,
+    use_active_mode: bool = False,
+    overwrite: bool = True,
+    tls: bool = False,
+) -> None:
+    """Opens a FTP connection with passed credentials, sets current directory
+    to the directory extracted from given path, then uploads the file to server.
+
+    If *tls* is ``True``, the connection is secured with TLS (FTPS), and the
+    certificate of the server is verified.
+    """
+    ftp = FTP_TLS(context=create_default_context()) if tls else FTP()
+    with ftp, closing(file):
+        ftp.connect(host, port)
+        ftp.login(username, password)
+        if isinstance(ftp, FTP_TLS):
+            ftp.prot_p()
+        if use_active_mode:
+            ftp.set_pasv(False)
+        file.seek(0)
+        dirname, filename = posixpath.split(path)
+        ftp_makedirs_cwd(ftp, dirname)
+        command = "STOR" if overwrite else "APPE"
+        ftp.storbinary(f"{command} {filename}", file)

@@ -0,0 +1,33 @@
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import signal
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from types import FrameType
+from typing import Any, TypeAlias
+
+# copy of _HANDLER from typeshed/stdlib/signal.pyi
+SignalHandlerT: TypeAlias = (
+    Callable[[int, FrameType | None], Any] | int | signal.Handlers | None
+)
+
+signal_names: dict[int, str] = {member.value: member.name for member in signal.Signals}
+
+
+def install_shutdown_handlers(
+    function: SignalHandlerT, override_sigint: bool = True
+) -> None:
+    """Install the given function as a signal handler for all common shutdown
+    signals (such as SIGINT, SIGTERM, etc). If ``override_sigint`` is ``False`` the
+    SIGINT handler won't be installed if there is already a handler in place
+    (e.g. Pdb)
+    """
+    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, function)
+    if (
+        signal.getsignal(signal.SIGINT)  # pylint: disable=comparison-with-callable
+        == signal.default_int_handler
+        or override_sigint
+    ):
+        signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, function)
+    # Catch Ctrl-Break in windows
+    if hasattr(signal, "SIGBREAK"):
+        signal.signal(signal.SIGBREAK, function)

+"""
+Module for processing Sitemaps.
+
+Note: The main purpose of this module is to provide support for the
+SitemapSpider, its API is subject to change without notice.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import warnings
+from io import BytesIO, StringIO
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
+from urllib.parse import urljoin
+
+import lxml.etree
+
+from scrapy.exceptions import ScrapyDeprecationWarning
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator
+
+
+class Sitemap:
+    """Class to parse Sitemap (type=urlset) and Sitemap Index
+    (type=sitemapindex) files"""
+
+    __slots__ = ("type", "xmliter")
+
+    def __init__(self, xmltext: str | bytes):
+        if isinstance(xmltext, str):
+            warnings.warn(
+                "Passing `str` type as `xmltext` is deprecated, use `bytes`",
+                ScrapyDeprecationWarning,
+                stacklevel=2,
+            )
+            xmltext = xmltext.encode()
+
+        self.xmliter = lxml.etree.iterparse(
+            BytesIO(xmltext),
+            recover=True,
+            remove_comments=True,
+            resolve_entities=False,
+            remove_blank_text=True,
+            collect_ids=False,
+            remove_pis=True,
+            events=("start", "end"),
+        )
+        _, root = next(self.xmliter)
+        self.type = self._get_tag_name(root)
+
+    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[dict[str, Any]]:
+        for event, elem in self.xmliter:
+            if event == "start":
+                continue
+
+            if self._get_tag_name(elem) not in {"url", "sitemap"}:
+                continue
+
+            if d := self._process_sitemap_element(elem):
+                yield d
+
+    def _process_sitemap_element(
+        self, elem: lxml.etree._Element
+    ) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
+        d: dict[str, Any] = {}
+        alternate: list[str] = []
+        has_loc = False
+
+        for el in elem:
+            try:
+                tag_name = self._get_tag_name(el)
+                if not tag_name:
+                    continue
+
+                if tag_name == "link":
+                    if href := el.get("href"):
+                        alternate.append(href)
+                else:
+                    d[tag_name] = el.text.strip() if el.text else ""
+                    if not has_loc and tag_name == "loc":
+                        has_loc = True
+            finally:
+                el.clear()
+        elem.clear()
+        parent = elem.getparent()
+        if parent is not None:
+            while elem.getprevious() is not None:
+                del parent[0]
+
+        if not has_loc:
+            return None
+
+        if alternate:
+            d["alternate"] = alternate
+
+        return d
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _get_tag_name(elem: lxml.etree._Element) -> str:
+        tag = elem.tag
+        if not isinstance(tag, str):
+            return ""
+        _, _, localname = tag.partition("}")
+        return localname or tag
+
+
+def sitemap_urls_from_robots(
+    robots_text: str | bytes,
+    base_url: str | None = None,
+) -> Iterable[str]:
+    if isinstance(robots_text, bytes):
+        for line in BytesIO(robots_text):
+            if line.lstrip()[:8].lower() == b"sitemap:":
+                try:
+                    url = line.partition(b":")[2].strip().decode()
+                except UnicodeDecodeError:
+                    continue
+                yield urljoin(base_url or "", url)
+
+    else:
+        warnings.warn(
+            "Passing `str` type as `robots_text` is deprecated, use `bytes`",
+            ScrapyDeprecationWarning,
+            stacklevel=2,
+        )
+        yield from _sitemap_urls_from_robots_str(robots_text, base_url)
+
+
+def _sitemap_urls_from_robots_str(
+    robots_text: str,
+    base_url: str | None = None,
+) -> Iterable[str]:
+    for line in StringIO(robots_text):
+        if line.lstrip()[:8].lower() == "sitemap:":
+            url = line.partition(":")[2].strip()
+            yield urljoin(base_url or "", url)

+"""Helper functions for working with templates"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+import string
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from os import PathLike
+
+
+def render_templatefile(path: str | PathLike[str], **kwargs: Any) -> None:
+    path_obj = Path(path)
+    raw = path_obj.read_text("utf8")
+
+    content = string.Template(raw).substitute(**kwargs)
+
+    render_path = path_obj.with_suffix("") if path_obj.suffix == ".tmpl" else path_obj
+
+    if path_obj.suffix == ".tmpl":
+        path_obj.rename(render_path)
+
+    render_path.write_text(content, "utf8")
+
+
+CAMELCASE_INVALID_CHARS = re.compile(r"[^a-zA-Z\d]")
+
+
+def string_camelcase(string: str) -> str:
+    """Convert a word  to its CamelCase version and remove invalid chars
+
+    >>> string_camelcase('lost-pound')
+    'LostPound'
+
+    >>> string_camelcase('missing_images')
+    'MissingImages'
+
+    """
+    return CAMELCASE_INVALID_CHARS.sub("", string.title())

+import importlib
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+
+from scrapy.exceptions import ScrapyDeprecationWarning
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("module_name", "names"),
+    [
+        (
+            "datatypes",
+            [
+                "CaseInsensitiveDict",
+                "LocalCache",
+                "LocalWeakReferencedCache",
+                "SequenceExclude",
+            ],
+        ),
+        ("display", ["pformat", "pprint"]),
+        ("ftp", ["ftp_makedirs_cwd", "ftp_store_file"]),
+        ("ossignal", ["SignalHandlerT", "install_shutdown_handlers", "signal_names"]),
+        ("sitemap", ["Sitemap", "sitemap_urls_from_robots"]),
+        (
+            "template",
+            ["CAMELCASE_INVALID_CHARS", "render_templatefile", "string_camelcase"],
+        ),
+    ],
+)
+def test_deprecated_module(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, module_name: str, names: list[str]
+) -> None:
+    old_path = f"scrapy.utils.{module_name}"
+    monkeypatch.delitem(sys.modules, old_path, raising=False)
+    with pytest.warns(
+        ScrapyDeprecationWarning, match=rf"The {old_path} module is deprecated\."
+    ):
+        old_module = importlib.import_module(old_path)
+    new_module = importlib.import_module(f"scrapy.utils._{module_name}")
+    assert sorted(old_module.__all__) == sorted(names)
+    for name in names:
+        assert getattr(old_module, name) is getattr(new_module, name)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "module_name",
+    [
+        "scrapy.cmdline",
+        "scrapy.crawler",
+        "scrapy.shell",
+        "scrapy.commands.fetch",
+        "scrapy.commands.genspider",
+        "scrapy.commands.parse",
+        "scrapy.commands.startproject",
+        "scrapy.extensions.feedexport",
+        "scrapy.pipelines.files",
+        "scrapy.spiders.sitemap",
+    ],
+)
+def test_no_deprecated_module_imports(module_name: str) -> None:
+    """Scrapy itself must not import the deprecated modules, as that would
+    show deprecation warnings to users."""
+    code = (
+        "import sys\n"
+        f"import {module_name}\n"
+        "deprecated = [m for m in ("
+        + ", ".join(
+            repr(f"scrapy.utils.{m}")
+            for m in ("datatypes", "display", "ftp", "ossignal", "sitemap", "template")
+        )
+        + ") if m in sys.modules]\n"
+        "assert not deprecated, deprecated\n"
+    )
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        [sys.executable, "-c", code], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False
+    )
+    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr

@@ -0,0 +1,47 @@
+import ctypes
+import platform
+import sys
+from pprint import pformat as pformat_
+from typing import Any
+
+from packaging.version import Version as parse_version
+
+
+def _enable_windows_terminal_processing() -> bool:
+    # https://stackoverflow.com/a/36760881
+    kernel32 = ctypes.windll.kernel32  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+    return bool(kernel32.SetConsoleMode(kernel32.GetStdHandle(-11), 7))
+
+
+def tty_supports_color() -> bool:
+    if sys.platform != "win32":
+        return True
+
+    if parse_version(platform.version()) < parse_version("10.0.14393"):
+        return True
+
+    # Windows >= 10.0.14393 interprets ANSI escape sequences providing terminal
+    # processing is enabled.
+    return _enable_windows_terminal_processing()
+
+
+def _colorize(text: str, colorize: bool = True) -> str:
+    # pylint: disable=no-name-in-module
+    if not colorize or not sys.stdout.isatty() or not tty_supports_color():
+        return text
+    try:
+        from pygments import highlight  # noqa: PLC0415
+    except ImportError:
+        return text
+    from pygments.formatters import TerminalFormatter  # noqa: PLC0415
+    from pygments.lexers import PythonLexer  # noqa: PLC0415
+
+    return highlight(text, PythonLexer(), TerminalFormatter())
+
+
+def pformat(obj: object, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
+    return _colorize(pformat_(obj), kwargs.pop("colorize", True))

index 000000000..f08e5303d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scrapy/utils/_ftp.py
@@ -0,0 +1,53 @@
+import posixpath
+from contextlib import closing
+from ftplib import FTP, FTP_TLS, error_perm
+from posixpath import dirname
+from ssl import create_default_context
+from typing import IO
+
+
+def ftp_makedirs_cwd(ftp: FTP, path: str, first_call: bool = True) -> None:
+    """Set the current directory of the FTP connection given in the ``ftp``
+    argument (as a ftplib.FTP object), creating all parent directories if they
+    don't exist. The ftplib.FTP object must be already connected and logged in.
+    """
+    try:
+        ftp.cwd(path)
+    except error_perm:
+        ftp_makedirs_cwd(ftp, dirname(path), False)
+        ftp.mkd(path)
+        if first_call:
+            ftp.cwd(path)
+
+
+def ftp_store_file(
+    *,
+    path: str,
+    file: IO[bytes],
+    host: str,
+    port: int,
+    username: str,
+    password: str,
+    use_active_mode: bool = False,
+    overwrite: bool = True,
+    tls: bool = False,
+) -> None:
+    """Opens a FTP connection with passed credentials, sets current directory
+    to the directory extracted from given path, then uploads the file to server.
+
+    If *tls* is ``True``, the connection is secured with TLS (FTPS), and the
+    certificate of the server is verified.
+    """
+    ftp = FTP_TLS(context=create_default_context()) if tls else FTP()
+    with ftp, closing(file):
+        ftp.connect(host, port)
+        ftp.login(username, password)
+        if isinstance(ftp, FTP_TLS):
+            ftp.prot_p()
+        if use_active_mode:
+            ftp.set_pasv(False)
+        file.seek(0)
+        dirname, filename = posixpath.split(path)
+        ftp_makedirs_cwd(ftp, dirname)
+        command = "STOR" if overwrite else "APPE"
+        ftp.storbinary(f"{command} {filename}", file)

+++ b/scrapy/utils/_ossignals.py
@@ -0,0 +1,33 @@
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import signal
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from types import FrameType
+from typing import Any, TypeAlias
+
+# copy of _HANDLER from typeshed/stdlib/signal.pyi
+SignalHandlerT: TypeAlias = (
+    Callable[[int, FrameType | None], Any] | int | signal.Handlers | None
+)
+
+signal_names: dict[int, str] = {member.value: member.name for member in signal.Signals}
+
+
+def install_shutdown_handlers(
+    function: SignalHandlerT, override_sigint: bool = True
+) -> None:
+    """Install the given function as a signal handler for all common shutdown
+    signals (such as SIGINT, SIGTERM, etc). If ``override_sigint`` is ``False`` the
+    SIGINT handler won't be installed if there is already a handler in place
+    (e.g. Pdb)
+    """
+    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, function)
+    if (
+        signal.getsignal(signal.SIGINT)  # pylint: disable=comparison-with-callable
+        == signal.default_int_handler
+        or override_sigint
+    ):
+        signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, function)
+    # Catch Ctrl-Break in windows
+    if hasattr(signal, "SIGBREAK"):
+        signal.signal(signal.SIGBREAK, function)

index 000000000..2edf2d5ef
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scrapy/utils/_sitemap.py
@@ -0,0 +1,129 @@
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import warnings
+from io import BytesIO, StringIO
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
+from urllib.parse import urljoin
+
+import lxml.etree
+
+from scrapy.exceptions import ScrapyDeprecationWarning
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator
+
+
+class Sitemap:
+    """Class to parse Sitemap (type=urlset) and Sitemap Index
+    (type=sitemapindex) files"""
+
+    __slots__ = ("type", "xmliter")
+
+    def __init__(self, xmltext: str | bytes):
+        if isinstance(xmltext, str):
+            warnings.warn(
+                "Passing `str` type as `xmltext` is deprecated, use `bytes`",
+                ScrapyDeprecationWarning,
+                stacklevel=2,
+            )
+            xmltext = xmltext.encode()
+
+        self.xmliter = lxml.etree.iterparse(
+            BytesIO(xmltext),
+            recover=True,
+            remove_comments=True,
+            resolve_entities=False,
+            remove_blank_text=True,
+            collect_ids=False,
+            remove_pis=True,
+            events=("start", "end"),
+        )
+        _, root = next(self.xmliter)
+        self.type = self._get_tag_name(root)
+
+    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[dict[str, Any]]:
+        for event, elem in self.xmliter:
+            if event == "start":
+                continue
+
+            if self._get_tag_name(elem) not in {"url", "sitemap"}:
+                continue
+
+            if d := self._process_sitemap_element(elem):
+                yield d
+
+    def _process_sitemap_element(
+        self, elem: lxml.etree._Element
+    ) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
+        d: dict[str, Any] = {}
+        alternate: list[str] = []
+        has_loc = False
+
+        for el in elem:
+            try:
+                tag_name = self._get_tag_name(el)
+                if not tag_name:
+                    continue
+
+                if tag_name == "link":
+                    if href := el.get("href"):
+                        alternate.append(href)
+                else:
+                    d[tag_name] = el.text.strip() if el.text else ""
+                    if not has_loc and tag_name == "loc":
+                        has_loc = True
+            finally:
+                el.clear()
+        elem.clear()
+        parent = elem.getparent()
+        if parent is not None:
+            while elem.getprevious() is not None:
+                del parent[0]
+
+        if not has_loc:
+            return None
+
+        if alternate:
+            d["alternate"] = alternate
+
+        return d
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _get_tag_name(elem: lxml.etree._Element) -> str:
+        tag = elem.tag
+        if not isinstance(tag, str):
+            return ""
+        _, _, localname = tag.partition("}")
+        return localname or tag
+
+
+def sitemap_urls_from_robots(
+    robots_text: str | bytes,
+    base_url: str | None = None,
+) -> Iterable[str]:
+    if isinstance(robots_text, bytes):
+        for line in BytesIO(robots_text):
+            if line.lstrip()[:8].lower() == b"sitemap:":
+                try:
+                    url = line.partition(b":")[2].strip().decode()
+                except UnicodeDecodeError:
+                    continue
+                yield urljoin(base_url or "", url)
+
+    else:
+        warnings.warn(
+            "Passing `str` type as `robots_text` is deprecated, use `bytes`",
+            ScrapyDeprecationWarning,
+            stacklevel=2,
+        )
+        yield from _sitemap_urls_from_robots_str(robots_text, base_url)
+
+
+def _sitemap_urls_from_robots_str(
+    robots_text: str,
+    base_url: str | None = None,
+) -> Iterable[str]:
+    for line in StringIO(robots_text):
+        if line.lstrip()[:8].lower() == "sitemap:":
+            url = line.partition(":")[2].strip()
+            yield urljoin(base_url or "", url)

@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+import string
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from os import PathLike
+
+
+def render_templatefile(path: str | PathLike[str], **kwargs: Any) -> None:
+    path_obj = Path(path)
+    raw = path_obj.read_text("utf8")
+
+    content = string.Template(raw).substitute(**kwargs)
+
+    render_path = path_obj.with_suffix("") if path_obj.suffix == ".tmpl" else path_obj
+
+    if path_obj.suffix == ".tmpl":
+        path_obj.rename(render_path)
+
+    render_path.write_text(content, "utf8")
+
+
+CAMELCASE_INVALID_CHARS = re.compile(r"[^a-zA-Z\d]")
+
+
+def string_camelcase(string: str) -> str:
+    """Convert a word  to its CamelCase version and remove invalid chars
+
+    >>> string_camelcase('lost-pound')
+    'LostPound'
+
+    >>> string_camelcase('missing_images')
+    'MissingImages'
+
+    """
+    return CAMELCASE_INVALID_CHARS.sub("", string.title())

title: Document `urlparse_cached()`?

judge.reasoning: Both patches make the identical, correct fix at the root: they add `.. autofunction:: scrapy.utils.httpobj.urlparse_cached` to the existing 'Other functions related to requests' section of request-response.rst, and both independent tests pass on both. The difference is in the docstring quality and tests. Patch A's docstring explains what is returned, that the cache is per-object (same ParseResult instance returned), that weak references mean objects are not kept alive, and includes a short worked example showing `.path` and `.netloc`, which directly mirrors the media-pipeline usage cited in the issue; the doctest values are correct. Patch B's docstring is also accurate and adds a useful 'prefer this over urlparse(x.url)' hint, but is shorter and has no example. Patch A additionally adds focused tests covering Response objects (previously only Request was tested) and the weak-reference non-retention property it now documents; these are non-tautological and exercise behavior the docstring claims, which is a reasonable accompaniment to a docs change rather than churn. The '1 line removed' in A's test file is just the import line being widened to include Response. Neither patch adds risk. On craft and tests A edges out B; correctness and scope are equal.

title: get_func_args_dict doesn't support PEP649 lazy annotation loading

judge.reasoning: Both patches fix the reported problem the same way: a `_signature` helper that passes `annotation_format=Format.FORWARDREF` on 3.14+, used in `get_func_args_dict` and in `_warn_spider_arg`. All five independent tests go from NameError on base to PASS on both, so correctness on the issue's scenarios is equal. The difference is in tests and scope. Patch A adds a small reusable helper (`tests/utils/pep649.py`) and exercises the fix at several levels: unit tests for `get_func_args_dict`/`get_func_args` with the issue's exact middleware shape, `_warn_spider_arg`, a real downloader-middleware run through the middleware manager (the user's actual use case), and a stats-collector regression. Patch B adds two narrower unit tests built around inline exec/compile. Both sets would fail before and pass after, and both are correctly skipped only below 3.14, where the bug cannot occur, so neither skip undermines the evidence. Patch A also rewrites `get_spec` on 3.14+ to avoid `getfullargspec`, which is beyond the issue's ask; it is carefully done (keeps bound `self`, ignores `__wrapped__`, filters to positional kinds, maps failures to TypeError like the stdlib) and gated to 3.14, so it adds modest risk but does not obscure the core fix. Patch B is tighter and has a nice touch documenting that `annotation` may now be a ForwardRef, but that craft edge does not outweigh A's materially stronger, scenario-level test coverage. Close call; A wins on tests, which rank above scope.

issue_md:
### Description
Hi scrapy team, in 3.14 `inspect.signature()` on type-annotated functions isn't safe at runtime as types are lazy in 3.14.

### Steps to Reproduce

```py
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    import scrapy


class SomeMiddleware:
    def process_exception(self, request: scrapy.Request, exception: Exception) -> None:
        pass

from scrapy.utils.python import get_func_args_dict

get_func_args_dict(SomeMiddleware().process_exception)  # crashes here
```

**Expected behavior:** 
`get_func_args_dict` returns (dict of arguments)

**Actual behavior:** 
Raises NameError: name 'scrapy' is not defined instead of returning. 

**Reproduces how often:** 
N/A / Always with Python 3.14

### Versions
```
Scrapy       : 2.17.0
lxml         : 6.1.1
libxml2      : 2.14.6
cssselect    : 1.5.0
parsel       : 1.11.0
w3lib        : 2.4.1
Twisted      : 26.4.0
Python       : 3.14.6 (main, Jun 23 2026, 15:46:31) [Clang 22.1.3 ]
pyOpenSSL    : 26.3.0 (OpenSSL 4.0.1 9 Jun 2026)
cryptography : 49.0.0
Platform     : macOS-26.5.2-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O
```

### Additional context
Found this when using `ruff`'s TC rules ([TC002](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/typing-only-third-party-import/)).

Potential fix for `annotation_format=inspect.Format.FORWARDREF` passed to inspect but not familiar enough with the codebase to say whether that's correct or not / what you do with the values downstream.

+def define_lazy(source: str, name: str, **namespace: Any) -> Any:
+    """Execute *source* without inheriting ``from __future__ import
+    annotations`` and return the object called *name* defined in it.
+
+    Annotations in *source* are thus lazily evaluated (PEP 649), which allows

title: Fix timezone handling in `FilesPipeline` stores

judge.reasoning: Both patches make the same correct S3/GCS fix (call `.timestamp()` on the tz-aware datetime instead of `time.mktime(dt.timetuple())`, which reinterpreted UTC wall-clock as local time), and both replace the FTP `float(MDTM)` nonsense with real `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS[.fff]` UTC parsing. The decisive difference is the FTP fractional-seconds edge. RFC 3659 allows an arbitrary number of fraction digits (`1*DIGIT`); Patch A's `_mdtm_to_timestamp` splits on '.' and parses the fraction with `float(f"0.{fraction}")`, so any length works. Patch B uses `strptime` with `%f`, which only accepts 1-6 digits; a longer fraction raises `ValueError`, which `stat_file`'s broad except swallows into `{}` (hence the independent test's `KeyError: 'last_modified'`), silently forcing a re-download. The independent tests confirm: A passes all 9, B fails `test_mdtm_reply_with_long_fraction`. On tests, A's `non_utc_local_timezone` fixture (TZ=+05:45 via tzset, skipped only where tzset is unavailable, i.e. Windows) makes the S3/GCS tests genuinely fail before the fix and asserts hard UNIX constants; its FTP tests cover plain and fractional MDTM against constants and tighten the real-server test to `approx(time.time())`. B's approach of feeding a +09:37-offset datetime is also a valid regression check and is portable, but its FTP test omits the >6-digit case its implementation breaks on. Scope is equivalent; craft slightly favors A's documented helper with doctest examples over inline conditional format selection. A is the better fix.

issue_md:
Found in https://github.com/scrapy/scrapy/pull/8182#discussion_r4053447020

Various `FilesPipeline` stores produce the `last_modifed` value as the UNIX timestamp and some or all of them may do it incorrectly, depending on what are the values returned by S3 and GCS and what is in FTP `MDTM`. Their tests may also hide these problems and may need to be improved.
